answer: Let trust propagate from independently anchored nodes by random walks of at most \(t\) steps on the weighted attestation graph, with voting weight proportional to the resulting walk mass. A Sybil cluster behind a sparse external cut of conductance \(\phi\) receives at most roughly \(t\phi\) of that mass from outside; its bridge therefore limits aggregate voting weight, even if an orchard of identities attest to one another internally. Min-cut transitivity bounds this leakage, while a narrow ridge of internal links cannot create external trust.
